verdicts.evidence: src/Scans/sibling_link.jl:23-42 removed the `break` after the first hit and now iterates every line with a `seen` flag, flagging a later line only when it links the site root (home_re), exempting a deep link to a named page. Verified by direct execution: a later mention on its own line that repeats the home link IS flagged (2-line and 3-line synthetic cases both produce the hit at the correct later line), while a later deep link produces no hit. src/Scans/sibling_link.jl:1-6 (module header) and :19-22 (function comment) were rewritten across commits 175fe95, 6f7f2b1 and 4205f77 to state exactly this behaviour, so the comment no longer overstates what the scan enforces.

class_surfaces.evidence: Module header rewritten from 'later mentions in the unit are bare code spans' (unchecked claim) to 'a later mention does not link the site again, though it may deep-link a named page of it' — now matches what sibling_link_hits! actually does.

The `break` after the first line is gone; a `seen` flag lets the loop keep scanning every remaining line for the same name and pushes a hit when a later line matches home_re. Confirmed by execution against synthetic 2- and 3-line inputs: a later home-link mention on its own line is caught (including with an intervening bare mention), a later deep link is correctly exempt.
